title: Coextension of scalars
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a monoidal category with equalizers. Assume it is closed: each
$X\otimes-$ has a right adjoint $\underline{\Hom}(X,-)$, with evaluation
$\mathrm{ev}\colon X\otimes\underline{\Hom}(X,Y)\to Y$. Let
$\varphi\colon\mathcal R\to\mathcal S$ be a morphism between monoid objects ([det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid]). No
commutativity or braiding is assumed. For an $\mathcal R$-module object $N$
([sk-def-sfb-module-objects]), let $\Hom_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal S,N)$ be the equalizer of
the two maps
$$
\underline{\Hom}(\mathcal S,N)\rightrightarrows\underline{\Hom}(\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal S,N).
$$
The first precomposes with the action
$\mu_{\mathcal S}(\varphi\otimes\mathcal S)\colon\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal S\to\mathcal S$.
The second is adjoint to
$\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal S\otimes\underline{\Hom}(\mathcal S,N)
\xrightarrow{\mathcal R\otimes\mathrm{ev}}\mathcal R\otimes N\xrightarrow{\gamma_N}N$.
Let $\mathcal S$ act on $\Hom_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal S,N)$ by right multiplication on the
source, $(s\cdot f)(t)=f(ts)$. That is, the action is adjoint to
$$
\mathcal S\otimes\mathcal S\otimes\Hom_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal S,N)
\xrightarrow{\mu_{\mathcal S}\otimes1}\mathcal S\otimes\Hom_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal S,N)
\to\mathcal S\otimes\underline{\Hom}(\mathcal S,N)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}}N .
$$
With postcomposition on morphisms, this defines the *coextension of scalars* functor
$\operatorname{Coext}_\varphi=\Hom_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal S,-)\colon
\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)$.

Here an equalizer of $p,q\colon H\rightrightarrows K$ means an object $E$ with a morphism $i\colon E\to H$ such that $pi=qi$, through which every $h\colon T\to H$ satisfying $ph=qh$ factors uniquely. The closed structure supplies natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X\otimes T,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(T,\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(X,Y))$. In the displayed action construction, first transpose with respect to the first $\mathcal S$ factor to obtain $\mathcal S\otimes E\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal S,N)$, and then take its unique factorization through the equalizer $E=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal S,N)$.

proof.text: Write $H_N=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(\mathcal S,N)$, $E_N=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal S,N)$, and $i_N\colon E_N\to H_N$ for the equalizer inclusion. Let $v_N=\mathrm{ev}\circ(1_{\mathcal S}\otimes i_N)\colon\mathcal S\otimes E_N\to N$, and $a=\mu_{\mathcal S}\circ(\varphi\otimes1_{\mathcal S})$. Uncurrying the equalizer equation gives $v_N\circ(a\otimes1_{E_N})=\gamma_N\circ(1_{\mathcal R}\otimes v_N)$, with associators inserted. The inclusion $i_N$ is monic directly by uniqueness in its universal property: if $i_Nu=i_Nw$, both $u,w$ are the factorization of that same equalizing map. Thus maps into $E_N$ can be compared by composing with $i_N$ and then uncurrying. Below expressions such as $v_N(t,e)$ are notation for these composites on ordered tensor factors, not an assumption that elements detect morphisms. Parentheses are changed only by associators.

proof.text: Transpose $v_N\circ(\mu_{\mathcal S}\otimes1_{E_N})$ with respect to the first $\mathcal S$ to get $k_N\colon\mathcal S\otimes E_N\to H_N$. It equalizes the defining pair: after uncurrying, the required equality on the ordered factors $\mathcal R,\mathcal S,\mathcal S,E_N$ is $v_N((\varphi(r)t)s,e)=v_N(\varphi(r)(ts),e)=\gamma_N(r,v_N(ts,e))$. The first equality is associativity of the monoid multiplication in [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid], and the second is the equalizer equation from step 1 precomposed with $1_{\mathcal R}\otimes\mu_{\mathcal S}\otimes1_{E_N}$. The equalizer universal property therefore defines the unique $b_N\colon\mathcal S\otimes E_N\to E_N$ with $i_Nb_N=k_N$. Its defining evaluation identity is $v_N(t,b_N(s,e))=v_N(ts,e)$.

source.place: Construction and well-definedness, expanded from the coextension clause of sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars

proof.text: The action $b_N$ obeys the module laws of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. To check the unit law, compose with $i_N$ and uncurry; the resulting equality is $v_N(t,b_N(1,e))=v_N(t1,e)=v_N(t,e)$, by the right unit law of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid]. For associativity the corresponding equality on ordered factors $t,s_1,s_2,e$ is $v_N(t,b_N(s_1,b_N(s_2,e)))=v_N(ts_1,b_N(s_2,e))=v_N((ts_1)s_2,e)=v_N(t(s_1s_2),e)=v_N(t,b_N(s_1s_2,e))$. Each equality uses the defining evaluation identity or the monoid associativity law. Injectivity of transposition and monicity of $i_N$ give the required two action equations, including their associators and unitors.

source.place: Construction and well-definedness, expanded from the coextension clause of sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars

proof.text: For a module morphism $g\colon N\to N'$, transpose $g\circ v_N$ to get $h_g\colon E_N\to H_{N'}$. It equalizes the defining pair for $E_{N'}$: on ordered factors $r,t,e$, $g(v_N(\varphi(r)t,e))=g(\gamma_N(r,v_N(t,e)))=\gamma_{N'}(r,g(v_N(t,e)))$. The last equality is exactly the module-morphism equation of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Define $E(g)\colon E_N\to E_{N'}$ by its unique equalizer factorization, so $v_{N'}(t,E(g)e)=g(v_N(t,e))$. This morphism is $\mathcal S$-linear because $v_{N'}(t,E(g)b_N(s,e))=g(v_N(ts,e))=v_{N'}(ts,E(g)e)=v_{N'}(t,b_{N'}(s,E(g)e))$. Comparison after $i_{N'}$ and transposition proves the equality of action maps. Finally $v_N(t,E(1)e)=v_N(t,e)$ and $v_{N''}(t,E(g'\circ g)e)=g'(g(v_N(t,e)))=v_{N''}(t,E(g')E(g)e)$ prove the identity and composition laws by the same uniqueness. This constructs the stated functor on objects and morphisms.
